title: BACE: Biotechnology Skills (Practical) - Biotechnology Skills - Cell Culturing
subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of the 'streak plate' method (e.g., T-streak or Quadrant streak)?
options: To count the exact number of bacteria in a sample.
To isolate single colonies from a mixed culture.
To grow a lawn of bacteria for antibiotic testing.
questions.explain: Streaking physically dilutes the inoculum across the agar surface to separate individual cells, which grow into isolated pure colonies.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: During a quadrant streak, what must you do between streaking each quadrant?
options: Dip the loop back into the original culture.
Add more antibiotic to the plate.
questions.explain: Flaming the loop between quadrants kills the bacteria on the loop, ensuring that the next quadrant is inoculated only by the small number of cells picked up from the edge of the previous streak (dilution effect).
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: What is the correct position for incubating Petri plates?
questions.explain: Plates are incubated upside down (inverted) to prevent condensation from forming on the lid and dripping onto the agar, which would smear the colonies.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Which growth phase is characterized by rapid exponential cell division?
questions.explain: Log phase (Logarithmic) is where the population doubles at a constant rate.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: What is the definition of a 'pure culture'?
options: A culture containing only one species of microorganism.
A culture that has been sterilized.
A culture containing bacteria and fungi.
A culture grown in a liquid broth.
questions.explain: A pure culture contains only a single species or strain, free from contaminants.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Which medium is solid and provides a surface for colony formation?
questions.explain: Agar is the solidifying agent. Broth is liquid.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: When performing a spread plate, what tool is typically used to distribute the sample?
questions.explain: An L-spreader (or 'hockey stick') is used to evenly spread the liquid sample across the entire surface of the agar.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: What visual characteristic helps distinguish different bacterial species on an agar plate?
options: The type of plastic dish used
questions.explain: Colony morphology involves the macroscopic characteristics (color, margin, elevation) used to identify bacteria.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Why is it important not to gouge the agar when streaking?
options: It disrupts the smooth surface, making colony isolation difficult and potentially trapping bacteria.
It changes the pH of the agar.
questions.explain: Gouging creates cracks where bacteria grow in clumps rather than isolated colonies, defeating the purpose of streaking.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: In the T-streak method, how many times do you pick up cells from the original source?
options: Only once, before the first streak.
Never, the loop is dipped in sterile water.
questions.explain: You inoculate only the first section from the source. Subsequent sections are inoculated by pulling cells from the previous section to dilute them.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: A culture tube with a loose cap is used to grow bacteria. Why is the cap kept loose?
options: To allow easy access for pipetting.
To allow gas exchange (oxygen) for aerobic bacteria.
To prevent the tube from exploding.
questions.explain: Aerobic bacteria require oxygen. A loose cap (or specialized vented cap) allows air in while keeping dust out.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Which temperature is most common for incubating human-associated bacteria like *E. coli*?
questions.explain: 37°C corresponds to human body temperature, which is the optimal growth temperature for mesophiles like *E. coli*.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills
